intended_object: A contracting homotopy for the mapping cone Cone(id_K) of the identity of a ℤ-indexed cochain complex K, i.e. a homotopy from the identity of Cone(id_K) to 0. This witnesses the standard fact that the cone of an identity map is contractible. Inferred from the docstring and from its use at line 418, where it shows that the cone is zero in the homotopy category.
explanation:
The type `Homotopy (𝟙 (mappingCone (𝟙 K))) 0` is exactly the data that makes the complex Cone(id_K) contractible: a homotopy between its identity and the zero map. Since the definition compiles, it has this type, so it gives such a homotopy. It is built with `descHomotopy` using the component `inl`, which matches the standard contracting homotopy (the map (k, k') ↦ (−k', 0), up to sign conventions).

The setting is the one in which Mathlib defines `mappingCone`: cochain complexes indexed by ℤ in a preadditive category with binary biproducts. So it is not too narrow.

This is mostly a witness used in a proof, but it is a genuine mathematical object (an explicit contracting homotopy), and it faithfully provides what the docstring claims.
